message.reasoning_content:
We need to determine crimes based on Chinese criminal law. Facts: Public servant (housing registration staff) accepted falsified documents, failed to verify, issued false property title, facilitating fraud, causing bank loss. Likely crimes: "受贿" no, no bribe. "徇私舞弊" maybe "国有资产犯罪"? Actually forging official documents: "伪造国家机关证件罪"? He didn't forge himself but accepted false documents and issued false property certificate. Could be "国有资产犯罪" - "非法占有、私分国有资产罪"? Not exactly. Could be "职务侵占罪"? He didn't appropriate property. He facilitated fraud: "帮助信息网络犯罪"? Not.

In Chinese law, a public official who, in performance of duties, knowingly accepts false documents and issues false certificates, causing loss, can be charged with "滥用职权罪" (abuse of power) or "徇私舞弊罪" (abuse of authority to commit fraud). The crime "徇私舞弊罪" (abuse of authority to commit fraud) is under Article 395 of Criminal Law (now 2020 amendment). It applies to state functionaries who, in performance of duties, accept bribes or accept false documents to facilitate illegal acts, causing losses. The description: "国家工作人员徇私舞弊，致使国家、集体或者他人财产遭受重大损失的，处三年以下有期徒刑或者拘役，并处罚金；情节特别严重的，处三年以上七年以下有期徒刑，并处罚金。" So likely "徇私舞弊罪".

Also possibly "伪造国家机关证件罪" but he didn't forge, he used false documents. The act of issuing false property certificate is "伪造国家机关证件罪" maybe because property certificate is a state-issued document. However the law says forging state documents is a crime. He didn't forge himself but allowed issuance of false certificate. Could be "伪造国家机关印章罪"? Not.

Thus likely charge: "徇私舞弊罪". Also maybe "信用卡诈骗罪" but that's for the borrower, not the official. The official's conduct is facilitating fraud, so "帮助信息网络犯罪"? No.

Thus answer: single crime: [罪名]徇私舞弊罪<eoa>
